rationale: B wins because it has the discipline to build around verifiable tension instead of decorating every supplied fact into an angle. Its "Sephora is betting more shelf on a brand whose numbers nobody outside can see" uses the private-company fact sharply; A's "Glossier times its first fragrance launch to its biggest retail push yet" is clever but smuggles in intent the update has not earned. A has real material, but B asks the harder reporter questions before the reporter does.
gaps_in_A: "Glossier times its first fragrance launch to its biggest retail push yet" over-claims intent. The update says the fragrance products launch alongside the expansion; it does not prove Glossier timed one to serve the other.

"fragrance-category dynamics — specifically why scent, unlike skincare or makeup, is a category that historically underperforms in pure DTC" imports an industry claim without evidence from the update.

"Sephora at Kohl's becomes a test case for prestige beauty in a big-box mall" turns one distribution inclusion into a category test case. That needs Sephora/Kohl's data, not just Glossier entering the footprint.
"mid-market and suburban shoppers" and "coastal-urban" invent a customer geography the update does not provide. Useful if store lists support it; sloppy if they do not.
gaps_in_B: "Sephora and LVMH's specialty-retail strategy" introduces LVMH even though the update never supplied it. True in the real world is not the same as grounded in this packet.
"DTC-native brands defend the direct relationship because it owns the customer data and the margin" is smart context, but it is still imported context. It needs sourcing before it becomes pitch copy.
"suburban strip-mall retail" and "suburban America" over-localize a North America rollout that includes Canada and unspecified locations.

B over-corrects on fragrance. "There is no scent, no perfumer, no price" is right for killing a product-review angle, but it misses the narrower retail-sampling strategy angle created by launching fragrance alongside the door expansion.
